decisions.question: Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: prop-wagon-shipment with its maps of 1024 px or more halved (resize_maps.py, then meshopt_glb.mjs; geometry, skin and clips byte-identical) is in the running game (board _reviews/gate3-resize-large). The file falls from 731,200 to 459,624 bytes. In isolated renders 0.038% of its pixels differ by more than 8/255 at 18 m (0.545% at pixel ratio 1.75, 0.0% at 26 m), tone ratio 0.9996; in the game (three factions, 18 and 26 m, pixel ratio 1 and 1.75) at most 0.019% of a frame differs by more than 8/255. Close-ups are softer (9.34% of pixels over 8/255). Shader programs are unchanged. Should I ship it?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.

supplementary.question: Gate 3 for batch C: the convoy wagon, Crown shipment, draft ox and cargo load are in the running game. The review board is open (127.0.0.1:47870), and you can play this branch's build at 127.0.0.1:47871. After the first captures, I fixed one defect. The pennant was edge-on from straight behind, so a hostile shipment's red nearly vanished. It's now enlarged and rippled, and it reads from behind. All wagon tests pass: 20/20, including every frame of every ox clip. All six deliberately broken copies are rejected, and the 9 browser tests pass. Measured cost: the site grows by 4.46 MB. On this GPU every scene is as fast or faster, and draw calls fall 30-65%. Triangles rise, so elf combat at high quality reaches 594k against the 400k budget. Under SwiftShader, frame time is within -2% to +5% of main. This is not AAA: the far sides and backs are invented; each body has a single painted albedo; the ox has cap hooves, painted eyes and a fused tail, and its gaits are procedural (canters at wagon speed); the shipment's glass is painted; and the pennant and canvas don't move. Do you approve delivery?

supplementary.question: Gate 3 re-ship, delegated under the standing instruction of 2026-10-01: all 23 shipped models, with their vertices and triangles reordered for locality and their geometry, skin and animation data compressed with EXT_meshopt_compression (no lossy filters), are in the running game (board 127.0.0.1:47896, _reviews/gate3-meshopt). Files fall 19.7% (23,330,396 to 18,733,460 bytes) and the gzip download GitHub Pages serves 6.9% (17,957,653 to 16,725,201 bytes), for 6,117 gzip bytes of decoder. Every model decodes to the same mesh, skin, clips and images; every frame-verifier metric is unchanged; of 213 game frames 200 are bit-identical and 13 differ in one pixel each; shader programs, draw calls (except +1-2 off-screen submissions in three shots), frame times and preload time show no measurable change. Should I ship the compressed models?

decidedBy.userMessage: Go ahead and since I approved all your recommended options before, go with your recommended options without asking for approval going forward.
